largeheadline_copy.line1: Know more. Ream less.1,2
largeheadline_copy.line2: The unique features of Mako Total Hip SmartRobotics™ are designed to help you optimize component positioning,1 enhance functional outcomes3 and elevate surgical experience.4,5

standaloneimage.alt: Image of surgeon and Mako Total Hip planning laptop

largeheadline_copy_c.line1: Know more.1
largeheadline_copy_c.line2: It all starts with a CT scan that creates a 3D image of your patient’s unique anatomy. Plan the sizing and positioning of implants, as well as incorporate Functional Hip Positioning™ to help you optimize component positioning.

text.text:
• CT-based platform to help optimize implant size and placement1

  • Plan implant center of rotation

  • Incorporate pelvic tilt analysis to understand the hip/spine relationship

  • Visualize and address potential impingement pre-operatively

  • Guided neck-resection tool

  • Hip length and offset feedback

largeheadline_copy_c_231302558.line2: With the use of AccuStopTM haptic technology, studies have demonstrated greater bone preservation,5 reduced blood loss6 and greater ability to reproduce hip biomechanics3,7-10  versus manual technique.

text.text:
• Ability to single stage ream

  • Ream constrained to planned center of rotation

  • Audible, visual and tactile feedback while guided reaming

  • Accurate bone preparation to plan20

  • Use of AccuStop™ haptic technology to help impact cup at the desired inclination and version3,6,8,11-12

largeheadline_282388331.line1: When it comes to the Direct Anterior (DA) Approach, where the field of view may be obscured and the use of fluoroscopy may be misleading, knowing more about a patient’s unique anatomy can make all the difference.15,16

text.text: Accurate and reproducible implant placement20

text_copy.text: Enhanced surgeon experience21,22

text_copy4806681511331920.text: Reduce, if not eliminate, fluoroscopy

largeheadline.line1: With Mako Total Hip, unlock planning features to help you know more about the femur-to-pelvis and component relationships.

standaloneimage.alt: Cup planning on Mako planning screen

text_copy.text: Surgeons can plan the cup size and position including inclination, version, and center of rotation.

standaloneimage_copy.alt: Stem planning on Mako planning screen

text_copy_copy.text: Surgeons can plan the stem position and visualize planned stem version based on the patient’s anatomy. Surgeons have the ability to choose what type of stem fits best from a cementless metaphyseal fit stem, tapered wedge stem or cemented stem.

standaloneimage_copy.alt: Pelvic tilt planning on Mako planning screen

text_copy_copy.text: Plan the placement of the cup based on the patient’s pelvic position in the supine, stand and seated pose.

standaloneimage_copy.alt: Virtual range-of-motion planning on Mako planning screen

text_copy_copy_copy.text: Visualize the femur-to-pelvis and component relationship in different patient positions (sitting/standing) to assess impingement preoperatively.

largeheadline_copy_1441688301.line1: Ream less2,3 with the AccuStop™ haptic technology of Mako Total Hip

text_copy_copy_copy.text: Allows surgeons to single-stage ream under haptic guidance to help achieve accurate bone preparation to plan.1-3,7-8,11-14

standaloneimage_copy.alt: Guided cup impaction on Mako screen

text_copy_copy_copy.text: Allows surgeons to implant the cup at the desired inclination and version.3,7-8,11-12

largeheadline_191797.line1:
Clinical success of Mako Total Hip
Based on 15 years of clinical data

largeheadline.line1:
Improved patient
outcomes

text.text: Studies have shown that Mako Total Hip patients are significantly less likely to be aware of their hip in daily circumstances compared to manual patients.6,9

largeheadline_copy_829891769480014781348.line1:
Less surgeon mental
and physical fatigue

text_copy.text: Mako Total Hip may reduce physical and mental demand for a surgeon that may lead to an improved surgical experience, especially while reaming, when compared to manual total hip arthroplasty.4,5

largeheadline_copy_84800273768186799.line1:
Reduced
dislocation rate

text_copy_copy.text: Studies have shown dislocation rates in Mako Total Hip are significantly reduced compared to manual patients.7,8

largeheadline_copy_8_5811078274800456449.line1:
Accurate restoration
of center of rotation

text_copy_copy.text: Center of rotation of the hip is more consistently replicated using Mako Total Hip compared to manual surgery.11

largeheadline_copy_8_6997503184801385576.line1:
Decreased length
of stay

text_copy_copy_copy.text: Mako Total Hip demonstrated a decreased length of stay compared to manual surgery.17

largeheadline_copy_8_8881218214801539507.line1:
Reduced
costs

text_copy_copy_copy_.text:
Mako Total Hip showed a reduced utilization of post index rehabilitation services such as skilled nursing home, health aid and impatient rehab.18

Mako Total Hip showed a reduced 90-day EOC costs compared to manual THA.18 Mako Total Hip showed reduced cumulative cost compared to manual THA for Medicare and private payer over 5 years.19
